submission.natural_language_explanation: Ignoring each text's first token, this pole is a retrospective token detector whose strength is set by the current token (94% of the variance of its pre-activation is between tokens, and it reads exactly the same 0.409 of max whatever token follows): it fires at about 0.15-0.7 of max on quantifiers and degree/discourse adverbs (most, much, another, either, every, each, less, almost, only, just, still, nearly, usually, generally, typically, especially, primarily), on relational prepositions and subordinators (under, after, before, between, into, when, if, while, than), on comparatives and superlatives (longest, best, greater, longer) and on abstract or procedural nouns and verbs (solution, role, result, influence, subject, challenge, standard, process, provide, involve, cover, ensure, require, follow, help, paper, said). It stays at the GELU floor (0.00 of max) on concrete everyday vocabulary - physical objects, animals, plants, foods, places and buildings (bed, cup, dog, egg, chair, flower, horse, fish, lake, street, snow), simple scalar adjectives (big, small, high, low, new, old, good, cold, hot, fast, slow, easy), basic everyday verbs (eat, sleep, sit, stand, open, close, buy, sell, pay, hold, keep, stop) - and on the highest-frequency glue plus 'plain' abstract words (that, this, is, about, at, from, by, idea, knowledge, reason, action, system, theory, method, value, social, national, important, really, also, actually), so an everyday sentence built only from those words peaks at or near zero (0.00-0.05 of max); the boundary is lexical rather than semantic and is graded, so a word just inside the firing families can sit anywhere from 0.1 to 0.5.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dog slept on the bed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An everyday sentence made only of a concrete animal, a concrete object and a basic verb from the hypothesis's floor list (sleep), so it predicts 0.00-0.05 of max.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A boy is on the bus. The bus is slow. The street is wet. A man has a bag of eggs and a box of bread. The bread is good. The eggs are cold. A woman is at the door of the shop. She has a cup and a plate. The plate is on the shelf. The shelf is high. A dog is in the yard. The yard is big. A cat is on the roof. The roof is old. The cat is small. Snow is on the roof. A fish is in the lake by the field. The lake is cold. A horse is in the field with a girl. The girl has a hat and a coat. The coat is new. The hat is old. A man is on the bed in the room. The room is cold. The bed is new. The fire is hot. The tea is good. The moon is high. A bird is in the tree. The tree is big. Sleep is good. Her idea is good. The method is easy.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long everyday passage built only from concrete objects, animals, foods, floor adjectives, basic verbs and the explicitly plain words idea/method, so the lexical hypothesis predicts it stays at the 0.00-0.05 floor even at length.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The idea is good and the method is easy.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Abstract nouns 'idea' and 'method' plus quality adjectives 'good' and 'easy' are explicitly listed as floor vocabulary, so the hypothesis predicts near-zero despite the surface resemblance to its abstract-noun firing family.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Their system is old and the theory is important.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'system', 'theory' and 'important' are named in the hypothesis's floor lists, so a sentence of plain abstract words should sit at 0.00-0.05 even though abstract nouns otherwise fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cat sat by the door of the shop.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relational prepositions 'by' and 'of' are not in the claimed firing set (under, after, before, between, into, when, if, while, than) and are listed as floor, so the hypothesis predicts near-zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The book is about a fish and a lake.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'about' is a semantically relational preposition but the hypothesis puts it in the high-frequency glue floor, and the content words are concrete, so it predicts 0.00-0.05.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Only the chair was new in the room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed firing token 'only' opens the text, where the first-token floor means it is never measured, and every later token is floor vocabulary, so the hypothesis predicts near-zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Most dogs sit and sleep all day.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed quantifier 'most' is at position 0 and unmeasured, the rest are floor verbs and nouns, and 'all' is a quantifier the hypothesis does not list, so it predicts near-zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The senator sat in a big chair and ate a hot dog.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A political sentence like example 3 but containing only a person noun, floor verbs and concrete objects (no year, said or will), so the lexical hypothesis predicts the floor and any firing would show semantic rather than token-level control.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He can buy a new car.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The modal 'can' is a near-miss for the claimed firing token 'will' and everything else is floor vocabulary, so the hypothesis predicts 0.00-0.05 and firing would show the family is modals rather than 'will'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: // Before committing, ensure each helper is small.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A code-comment context containing claimed firing items ('before', 'ensure', 'each'), so the hypothesis predicts 0.15-0.7 despite the non-prose setting and absent example vocabulary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He said, "It is still raining between the hills."
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dialogue using the claimed firing tokens 'said', 'still' and a spatial 'between', a new genre and a physical rather than abstract relation, all predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The team played longer than anyone expected, and the coach said they would return.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sports commentary using the comparative 'longer', the subordinator 'than' and the verb 'said', claimed firing tokens in a context unlike any of the provided examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The research team typically requires every participant to provide a sample.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A scientific-register paraphrase packing the claimed firing tokens 'typically', 'requires', 'every' and 'provide' with none of the exact example wording, predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Look there, under the old bridge by the mill.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed activating tokens 'there' and 'under' in an otherwise purely concrete everyday scene, which the token-level hypothesis still predicts fires at 0.15-0.7.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The office is on the third floor of a tall building. A man in a grey coat walks in at eight and sits at a desk by the window. He has a phone and a pen. A woman at the desk in front of him has a drawer of pens and a pile of letters. The room is cold. The light is low. A clock on the wall is old. At nine the people sit at a big table in the middle of the room. A girl writes on a card and passes it down the table. The card is small. Nobody speaks. A guard sleeps by the door. At noon they eat at the desk. The phone rings and a woman answers it. She writes a note and puts it in a drawer. The drawer is on the left. A man in a blue coat comes in at one with a bag of tools. He sits on a chair and opens the bag. The tools are old. He holds a small piece and a pen. The light is low. The room is cold. At three the woman in the grey coat stands up and walks to the door. She gets on a bus. The bus is slow. At four a boy brings a box of forms and puts it on the desk. He has a small key and a card. A girl in a red coat walks to the shelf and takes a box of pens. She puts the box on the table. The clock on the wall is old. The phone rings again and nobody answers it. At five the people at the table put the pens in a drawer and go home. The office is dark. The bus in the street is slow. Snow is on the roof of the building. At the end of the week the manager will follow the usual process to cover the cost of the pens, and the staff must provide a list of the parts they need.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The only claimed firing vocabulary ('will', 'follow', 'process', 'cover', 'provide') appears roughly 300 tokens into an otherwise floor-vocabulary office narrative, testing that a token detector keyed to the current token fires on a deep token rather than on position or context length.
